description: #749 adjacency-is-not-flow and operand-isolation negative controls: an adjacent untrusted-source assignment whose target the construction never uses (request_id near a constant join), an untrusted token with no assignment target at all, an assignment LHS containing request vocabulary (request_cache_path), a static quoted word adjacent to an anchor call (label = "request"), a trailing COMMENT containing request vocabulary, a SIBLING statement donating request.id after a static join, a BARE filename identifier (trusted constant propagated into a path), and — for multi-line constructions — a comment after the closing paren, a sibling statement after the closer, and a comment on the open-call head line are all trusted/clean — path_handling must not fire and the provenance artifact stays empty. Only the construction call's balanced operand list is scanned; co-occurrence never substitutes for the one-hop def/use edge. Additionally, word-bounded source vocabulary: benign identifier near-misses (requester_id, username, queryset, payloads) as construction operands are clean, and a trusted pathlib division (Path(__file__).parent / "static") does not fire. Division operands end at the statement boundary: a sibling expression after the `/` division of a static path cannot donate untrusted tokens.
